label: input token g during the original (pre-delimiter) phase
explanation: Fires on essentially every step where the input token is the letter g in the original phase (t < L), at any position and for any sequence length, with fairly uniform magnitude (mean 0.62, median 0.61 of max 0.74). It does not fire on the delimiter step or when g is fed back as input in the copy phase (only ~100 tiny residual activations, about 0.15 of max, at the step right after <DEL> echoing g at recall_idx 1). No other token activates it. Magnitude is somewhat higher when g is the first occurrence and the top examples are often preceded by q within the last few tokens, but variation is small; the feature is effectively a binary detector of original-phase g.

issues: Every factual claim held up. Test precision is 1.0, recall 0.9988, F1 0.9994, mass recall 0.9998. No step where the predicate is true goes inactive.

The feature is silent on the delimiter step (0 of 500k). In the copy phase it fires on only 108 dev steps, all with zero activation mass, and 100 of those are at recall_idx 1, where g is echoed right after <DEL>, at about 0.15 of max. This is a tiny low-magnitude echo, not a systematic class that matters.
Position, length and to_go make no difference: about 0.033-0.034 per orig_idx and a lift of 1.0x across L and to_go. Other tokens are negligible: only digits 2 and 0 fire, 17 activations in total.

The test misses (126 steps) follow the same pattern: the post-<DEL> g echo plus a few digit steps at about 0.15 of max, with 0.0% of the mass. This is scattered or negligible, and the label does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
